projects_read.title: See sites
projects_read.description: List the sites you pick below.

content_read.title: Read files
content_read.description: Read content, schemas and history, and clone the repository.

content_write.title: Edit content
content_write.description: Create, edit and delete files in the content and config folders.

media_write.title: Manage media
media_write.description: Upload, rename and delete files in the media folder.

schema_write.title: Edit schemas
schema_write.description: Change schemas and snippets in .sitepins. Changing .sitepins/config.json needs Edit code.

code_write.title: Edit code
code_write.description: Change any other file, such as templates and package.json. CI workflow files are never writable.

git_branch.title: Branches and pull requests
git_branch.description: Commit to other branches and open pull requests.

fields.projects_all_description: Every site in this organization, including ones added later.
fields.no_projects: This organization has no sites yet.
fields.write_direct_description: Changes go straight to the site's branch, committed by the Sitepins bot.
fields.write_pull_request_description: Changes go to a new branch with a pull request for you to review.

settings.title: MCP Connection
settings.description: Give AI agents like Claude, Codex, Cursor and Antigravity access to your sites. Create a token, then paste the setup prompt into your agent. Their commits come from the Sitepins bot.
settings.connect_description: Copy this prompt and paste it into your AI agent. It adds Sitepins to the agent's MCP settings. The token is shown only once.
settings.revoke_description: It loses access right away. Changes it already committed stay in the repository.
settings.create_description: Choose which sites the agent can reach and what it may change.

editor.external_commit: {name} changed this file via {agent}. Publishing will show you what changed first.
